routes.name: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
routes.fit: A first broad cybersecurity credential for a newcomer.
routes.eligibility: No work experience is required. Follow ISC2's current identity, exam and ethics policies. Self-study is possible; completing this hub is not an entry requirement or a guarantee of passing.
routes.exam: Register with ISC2, then schedule the exam at an authorised Pearson testing centre. The current CC outline uses a two-hour adaptive exam with 100–125 items. Check the latest outline and local appointments before paying.
routes.after: After passing, complete the certification application and ethics agreement, then pay the applicable annual maintenance fee. CC maintenance includes 45 CPE credits over three years. Passing alone is not the final award step.
routes.cost: Budget for the current regional exam price, travel, any retake and recurring maintenance. Check offers with ISC2; do not assume an earlier free-exam campaign still applies.
routes.gap: Download the current official exam outline and compare every objective. Add exam-specific study and legitimate practice questions, especially governance, continuity and operational terminology. This topic selection is a study suggestion, not a complete approved exam mapping.

routes.name: INE eJPT — Junior Penetration Tester
routes.fit: A practical entry route when you prefer authorised penetration-testing work.
routes.eligibility: INE describes this as entry level; practical networking and systems knowledge is expected. Its published voucher route requires an INE Fundamentals subscription. Verify the current purchase terms in your own account.
routes.exam: Use the official objectives and designated lab preparation, buy the required voucher and complete the practical exam under its rules. The provider currently describes a 180-day voucher window; confirm attempt and retake deadlines before purchase.
routes.after: The credential is valid for three years under the published provider policy. Check the current renewal route directly; do not assume a lifetime award.
routes.cost: Account for subscription plus voucher and the exact included attempts, access window and renewal costs. The native exercises do not replace experience in INE's authorised hands-on environments.
routes.gap: The exam also expects practical host/network assessment skills and tools beyond the hub's paper fixtures. Follow the provider's current objectives and lab path before booking. Never practise those techniques on unapproved systems.

routes.name: GIAC Security Essentials (GSEC)
routes.fit: A broader practitioner option for someone with IT and networking foundations; compare its total budget carefully.
routes.eligibility: SANS training is not required for GIAC certification. Review GIAC's registration terms and objectives; passing a training course is not the same as passing the independent exam.
routes.exam: Apply/register through GIAC and take the proctored exam. GIAC publishes remote and testing-centre delivery options. The current page lists 106 questions in four hours, with a 120-day window after activation; the attempt-specific rules in your account govern.
routes.after: GIAC credentials renew every four years. The current route permits 36 CPEs or renewal by exam, plus a maintenance fee. Maintain evidence of eligible activities.
routes.cost: Compare exam-only registration with any optional SANS training. Include proctoring/attempt terms, retakes, materials and renewal in the total; this can be a substantially different purchase from an introductory exam.
routes.gap: Use the current GSEC objectives to close platform, administration and hands-on task gaps. The hub's examples support foundations; they are not a GIAC-endorsed preparation package.

routes.name: ISC2 CISSP — a later experience-based route
routes.fit: A later professional goal for broad security responsibility, rather than the first exam a beginner needs.
routes.eligibility: Full certification normally requires five cumulative years of qualifying experience across at least two CISSP domains. A qualifying degree or approved credential may waive one year under ISC2's rules. Experience must be documented; self-study hours are not a substitute.
routes.exam: Self-study can prepare you for the exam. Someone who passes without the required experience may pursue Associate of ISC2 status and then meet its experience deadline. That person must not claim to hold CISSP until all award requirements are met.
routes.after: Complete the applicable application/endorsement and ethics steps. Full CISSP maintenance includes 120 CPE credits over three years and an annual fee. Review the current rules for your status.
routes.cost: Budget for the current regional exam price, preparation, retakes if needed and recurring maintenance. Confirm experience eligibility and the Associate route before choosing an exam date.
routes.gap: This hub does not supply the required professional experience or cover every CISSP objective. Use the current official outline and maintain real work evidence with your employer or relevant organisation.
